subject: Short/truncated generations reported by BlueCart - investigation
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex@bluecart.com>
To: support@redwood.com; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short/truncated generations observed in production

Hi team,

We're seeing a handful of production requests over the last 36 hours where the model returns a very short or seemingly truncated response (1-3 tokens) instead of the expected paragraph. Examples attached (sample_prompt.json) and the raw request/response traces are in bluecart_request-logs.txt.

Examples:
- request_id: bc-20270413-09:14 -> response: "Ok."
- request_id: bc-20270414-02:07 -> response: "Sure."

We've validated client-side logic and retries are not being triggered on our side. Calls use redwood-hosted endpoint in us-west, model: open-gpt-7b-quant. These events are intermittent (roughly 0.03% of traffic) and non-deterministic.

Can you confirm whether there's any known degradation or whether these match any internal throttles/batching behavior? Logs attached. Happy to provide additional traces.

Thanks,
Alex Nguyen
SRE, BlueCart Retail
alex@bluecart.com

Attachments: bluecart_request-logs.txt, sample_prompt.json

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@bluecart.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:45:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Short/truncated generations observed in production

Hi Alex — thanks for the report and for attaching the logs. We're looking into this. Quick questions that will help narrow scope:

- Can you confirm whether the short responses are always exactly the first token(s) of the expected output, or appear as unrelated short phrases?
- Are you using streaming responses or the standard complete-generation endpoint?
- Do you have a couple of request_ids you want us to prioritize?

I've looped in Vivek (on infra/runtime) and our on-call infra (Ben). We'll attempt to reproduce with the exact prompt and model configuration you sent. If possible, please reply with one recent request_id you saw during a peak window.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:20:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Short/truncated generations observed in production (internal)

Marking internal triage notes here. I attempted reproduction against open-gpt-7b-quant in us-west using the sample_prompt.json (replication harness attached to ticket). Summary:

- Ran 2500 requests over a range of sequence lengths and temperature settings. Did not observe 1-3 token truncations. Median latency and token counts within expected distribution.
- Checked node-level logs and runtime metrics during the windows Alex indicated; no OOMs, no fast-kill events, and no runtime-level exceptions.
- KV cache / batching telemetry shows healthy batching sizes; no abrupt batch flushes that would explain truncated outputs.
- Searched for any recent kernel or runtime changes affecting token emission; none deployed to us-west between 2027-04-12 and 2027-04-14.

Hypothesis: client-side early-close / network-level resets or a malformed prompt that reduces decoding length. Also possible client-side middleware (proxy) returning early.

I'll attach internal triage notes (redwood-internal-triage-notes.md) to the ticket and continue targeted reproductions using the BlueCart request_id list if Alex provides them.

—Ben (On-call Infra)
Ben Carter
Senior Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@bluecart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short/truncated generations observed in production — investigation summary

Hi Alex — following up with our investigation summary and next steps. Thank you for sending the logs and sample prompt. High-level findings: 

1) Reproduction: our internal reproductions (Ben's runs) with the exact sample prompt and model did not produce truncated / 1-3 token responses. We ran 2500+ tests across temperatures and prompt wrappers.

2) Platform telemetry: no runtime errors, OOMs, or kernel-level faults noted in the specified windows (us-west). Batching and KV cache signals look nominal. No configuration changes or rollouts that coincide with BlueCart's timestamps.

3) Likely causes we considered and guidance:
   - client/network: intermittent connection resets or proxies that terminate the body and surface the first token back to the caller. Please ensure the client is not closing the response stream early (especially for streaming responses).
   - prompt engineering: very short system messages or truncation in the last token of the prompt can bias generation length; if you have prompt preprocessing, try disabling that as a test.
   - retry/duplicate wiring: if middleware retries incorrectly, an earlier short response (from a warmup/test) could be served back.

Action taken: opened ticket INF-4821 and attached our reproduction harness and triage notes (redwood-internal-triage-notes.md). We're happy to run targeted reproductions if you share a few concrete request_ids or a short sample window. For now, given no platform evidence, we consider the incident as "not confirmed on Redwood" but remain open to re-open if new traces demonstrate server-side errors.

Next steps for your team (suggestion):
- Provide 2-3 request_ids with exact timestamps so we can do a side-by-side trace.
- If using streaming: switch to a single non-streamed request for a quick test to see if result length changes.
- Check any edge proxies/ingress (e.g., cloud CDN, internal middleware) for early connection closes.

If you'd like, we can schedule a short joint debug session (30 min) where we run the call live and watch traces together.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll keep the ticket open and can escalate to an expanded postmortem if we find a reproducible server-side cause.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Reliability | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com
